name: soapysdr
desc: Vendor and platform neutral SDR support library
why: A vendor-neutral SDR abstraction that opens the door to a huge range of radio hardware.

brief.what_it_is: SoapySDR is an open-source, vendor-neutral API and runtime library for software-defined radio hardware. A program opens a device, configures it, and streams samples to or from it through one common interface, whatever the hardware vendor. Hardware support comes from runtime-loadable driver modules (plugins), and the wiki says most off-the-shelf SDR hardware is covered. The library has bindings for C, C++, Python, Go, Rust, LuaJIT and .NET, and it is used as the hardware layer by many SDR applications. The brew formula ships a command-line tool called SoapySDRUtil.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki says the project exists to give platform creators and application authors one way to talk to the general class of SDR devices (RF front end, ADC/DAC, PC interface) without getting lost in each vendor's details. It also lets vendors ship their own driver module alongside their driver package.
brief.how_it_works: Client code uses the SoapySDR::Device class (or the C, Python or other wrapper) to find, instantiate, configure and stream from a device. Drivers are separate runtime-loadable modules that implement discovery and a factory function for their hardware, so they can be installed without recompiling the platform. The wiki also describes remote access, which carries any supported device over a local network link.

commands_seen.context: Example from the wiki's Plugin architecture section: sets an extra directory to search for installed SoapySDR driver modules. The path shown is only an example.

brief.install_notes: The wiki says prebuilt binaries are on the Pothos downloads page for Windows, OSX, Ubuntu and OpenSUSE, or you can build from source following the build guide (not fetched). Building the core needs only a C++ compiler and CMake. Vendor driver modules and language bindings may bring in their own dependencies. Driver modules are loaded at runtime, so they can be added later without rebuilding SoapySDR. The README itself gives no install commands; the brew install is a Homebrew formula.
brief.standout: Its driver model is the notable part: vendors ship a runtime-loadable module against an installed SoapySDR, and applications such as GNU Radio, GQRX, SDR++ and Pothos reach hardware through that single API. The wiki also says the same plugin mechanism can carry network remoting and Python or Go bindings.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The wiki home page was last edited Sep 29, 2026 across 67 revisions, and the repo README shows a CI build-status badge. I did not see a release date or latest commit date, so the exact release cadence is unknown.
brief.caveats: The README is very short and defers nearly everything to the wiki, and the build guide, driver guide and remote-access pages were not followed. The wiki says SoapySDR is not meant to be a general hardware abstraction library; it targets SDR devices. Licensing: the core is under the Boost Software License 1.0 per the README, but the wiki asks users to respect the separate licences of platform and vendor driver software. Hardware coverage depends on which driver modules are installed.
quotes: A fresh and clean vendor neutral and platform independent SDR support library
SoapySDR supports SDR devices through runtime-loadable modules.
Use any SoapySDR supported device transparently over a local network link.
